ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog is brown or grey with distinct white spots and a granular back. It features large, dark-pigmented toe pads and a pale, mottled belly. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Theloderma albopunctatum* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, raised white tubercles scattered across its dorsum, which contrast sharply with its skin.
ai.habitat: This frog inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near tree holes or water-filled cavities at altitudes of 400–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Dotted Bubble-nest Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation near forest pools and streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Theloderma albopunctatum* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes or rock cavities.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Theloderma albopunctatum* occurs in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Meghalaya) at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Dotted Bubble-nest Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "peep" or "chirp" notes, typically heard from vegetation surrounding forest pools.
